subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should OpenClaw allow credential-shaped keys from `skills.entries.<skill>.env` to reach host `exec`, and if so should that be limited to declared skill env names or to a skill-scoped execution path?
rationale: The source-backed availability bug is real, but the straightforward fix conflicts with an open security issue about skill secrets leaking to unrelated exec children, so automation cannot choose the permanent boundary safely.

options.title: Add scoped skill-exec env
options.body: Permit sensitive keys only for the skill invocation or a declared skill env contract, and keep generic exec from inheriting unrelated active skill secrets.

options.title: Require metadata declarations
options.body: Ask bundled and third-party skills to declare sensitive env names in `metadata.openclaw.requires.env`, which minimizes core policy change but leaves arbitrary user-configured sensitive env blocked.

options.title: Keep fail-closed
options.body: Preserve the current block, document the supported top-level/sandbox env alternatives, and accept that some headless skill auth flows remain manual.

recommendation.title: Add scoped skill-exec env
recommendation.body: Permit sensitive keys only for the skill invocation or a declared skill env contract, and keep generic exec from inheriting unrelated active skill secrets.

likelyOwner.reason: `vincentkoc` is the best available routing owner from the evidence because recent work spans the current checkout, exec/Codex approval security, and the bundled `gog` skill surface.
